jobs.title: Director, Finance Technology Solutions and Products
jobs.description:
WHAT DOES AGNICO EAGLE VALUE?

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? Because they express who we are, and they have helped us succeed in business for over 60 years. We value you
– your unique set of skills and experience. We value your willingness to build those skills and make a meaningful contribution to our company. And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

About Our Operation

Canadian-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983.

Want to learn more about our operations and projects? Click here!

Your Next Challenge

Reporting to the Corporate Director, Finance Technology, you will be part of the Finance Department. You will provide product leadership for Finance Technology, translating strategy into an integrated roadmap and driving execution, adoption and continuous improvements across the organization. Your decision's will impact the company’s finance capabilities across Agnico Eagle’s global portfolio. You will enable the Company to operate more efficiently, generate better insights, and make faster, more informed decisions.

In this hands-on leadership role, you will lead a team while working closely with business stakeholders from Operations, Finance and IT to translate business needs into scalable technology solutions. You will drive capabilities across budgeting and forecasting, long-range planning, reporting, automation, advanced analytics and AI.

End-to-End product ownership and execution within the Finance Technology strategy
Drives the product, translates finance needs into priorities, coordinates delivery and is accountable for the execution and outcomes
Serve as a key member of the Finance Technology leadership team, providing strategic advice and recommendations to the Corporate Director and VP on product strategy, investment priorities, technology capabilities and governance.
Own the product roadmap and backlog
Drive adoption and realization of expected benefits
Own stakeholder engagement and product governance processes
Accountable for the daily decisions to drive the product(s)

Partner with business leaders to identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve Finance-related processes
Requires enterprise-wide stakeholder management and balancing competing priorities across Finance, Technology and the needs of operations.
Lead product delivery from business requirements and prioritization through solution design, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement
Own and evolve Finance capabilities across budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, reporting, automation, advanced analytics and AI
Identify and prioritize AI and advanced analytics opportunities for Finance, leveraging Databricks in partnership with Data and Technology teams
Ensure Finance solutions are supported by trusted, governed, and integrated data
Manage competing priorities and ensure investments are aligned with business value and strategic objectives
Lead and develop a Product Owner team while remaining actively involved in key initiatives.
Communicate product strategy, progress, risks, and outcomes to senior Finance and Technology stakeholders

What You Need To Succeed

Bachelor’s Degree in finance, IT or other relevant field of study required.
CPA, MBA, or technology related specialisation.
Knowledge of the mining industry is considered an asset.
15+ years of progressive experience in Finance Technology, Finance Transformation, product management, enterprise applications, or related areas.
Strong understanding of finance processes, including budgeting, long-range planning, forecasting, management reporting, and performance management.
Experience leading complex technology products or Finance transformation initiatives.
Knowledge of EPM, ERP, enterprise data platforms, analytics, automation, and AI technologies.
Familiarity with JD Edwards, Anaplan, Hyperion or similar is considered an asset.
Experience with Databricks or similar modern data and analytics platforms is an asset.
Strong product management, stakeholder engagement, and prioritization skills.
Demonstrated ability to operate at both a strategic and hands-on delivery level.
Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving capabilities.
Proficiency of the French language is considered an asset.

Your Work Schedule

Schedule: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday from our Corporate office in Toronto, ON.

jobs.description:
Req Id:

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Program Director, you will be accountable for the end-to-end delivery of the national data centre build program—orchestrating scope, schedule, budget, and cross-functional execution across multiple concurrent sites. You'll be the integrating force connecting construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls into one predictable, well-governed program, ensuring Bell delivers these mission-critical facilities on time, on budget, and to standard as the initiative scales aggressively nationally.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for the national data centre build program, integrating scope, schedule, budget, and quality across multiple concurrent sites.
Orchestrate cross-functional execution across construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls, ensuring alignment to program objectives.
Establish and govern the program delivery framework—stage gates, milestones, governance cadence, and decision rights—across the portfolio.
Own the integrated master schedule and program-level budget, driving predictability, transparency, and schedule discipline across all builds.
Lead program-level risk management, change governance, and interdependency management, escalating and resolving systemic issues before they impact delivery.
Provide executive-level program reporting to AI Fabric and Capital Programs leadership, translating complex delivery status into clear, decision-ready insight.
Manage program financials, forecasting, and capital planning in partnership with finance and program controls.
Drive resource planning and prioritization across sites, balancing competing demands as the program scales
Build and mature Bell's program delivery capability at a formative stage, embedding repeatable processes, playbooks, and lessons learned across the fleet.
Serve as a senior point of escalation and executive interface for site directors, functional leads, and external delivery partners.

Critical Qualifications

15+ years leading large-scale capital program delivery, with direct experience on hyperscale or mission-critical data centres (multi-site / multi-billion-dollar portfolios preferred)
Proven track record owning end-to-end program delivery across multiple concurrent construction projects, not just single-project management.
Deep command of program management disciplines—integrated master scheduling, budget/cost control, risk management, and change governance.
Strong understanding of the full data centre delivery lifecycle—construction, engineering, MEP, and commissioning through to operational handover.
Demonstrated ability to integrate and align diverse cross-functional teams and external delivery partners.
Expertise in program governance, stage-gate frameworks, and executive reporting.
Exceptional executive presence, able to influence and challenge senior engineering, construction, finance, and executive leaders.
Experience building and maturing a program delivery organization from a formative stage.
Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related discipline; PMP/PgMP, P.Eng., or equivalent strongly preferred.
Willingness to travel nationally between build locations as the portfolio scales.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.title: Technology Director
jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The lululemon cybersecurity team helps protect the trust our guests, employees, and partners place in us. We work across technology and the business to understand risk, build practical security capabilities, and enable teams to move quickly and responsibly. We are looking for a Director of Security Operations to lead our Security Incident Response Team (SIRT), Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and Detection Engineering capabilities. This leader will build an operation that treats detections as software: versioned, tested, measurable, and continuously improved.

Core Responsibilities

You will lead a global team of security engineers, analysts, threat hunters, intelligence practitioners, and incident responders. You will set the strategy and operating model for detecting, investigating, and responding to threats across lululemon’s technology environment. You are as comfortable discussing telemetry and detection logic with engineers as you are explaining business impact and response decisions to executives. You know that effective security operations is not measured by how many alerts a team can generate. It is measured by how reliably we identify meaningful threats, respond to them, and improve the systems around us.

Lead incident response

Own the SIRT strategy, incident response lifecycle, and operational readiness across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, network, and application environments.
Lead coordination during significant incidents, establishing clear decision-making, escalation, communications, and recovery processes.
Partner with technology teams, Legal, Privacy, Communications, Risk, and other stakeholders to manage incidents and their business impact.
Run exercises and post-incident reviews that result in owned, tracked improvements to detection, response, and resilience.
Establish a sustainable global coverage model, including on-call and external partnerships where appropriate.

Build detection as code

Set the direction for a detection engineering program that manages detection logic, queries, rules, and response workflows as version-controlled code.
Establish engineering practices for peer review, automated testing, deployment, documentation, tuning, and retirement of detections.
Use threat modeling, incident learnings, threat intelligence, and adversary behavior to prioritize detection coverage against meaningful risks.
Validate detections continuously through simulation, replay, purple teaming, and other appropriate testing methods.
Reduce alert fatigue by improving signal quality, enriching context, and automating repeatable work while retaining human judgment for consequential decisions.

Own security observability

Define the telemetry strategy needed to investigate threats across identities, systems, applications, cloud services, and data flows.
Partner with engineering and platform teams to build reliable, secure, and cost-conscious telemetry pipelines, including clear ownership, data quality, retention, and access controls.
Identify and address visibility gaps, including those created by changes in infrastructure, SaaS adoption, and emerging technologies.
Guide the evolution and consolidation of security operations tooling, including decisions about what to build, buy, retain, or retire.

Turn intelligence into action

Lead a threat intelligence capability that identifies and communicates threats relevant to lululemon’s business, technology, and operating environment.
Translate intelligence into prioritized detections, hunts, defensive improvements, and incident readiness.
Build trusted relationships with industry peers, partners, and relevant information-sharing communities.

Build the team and program

Hire, develop, and retain a diverse, high-performing team. Create clear career paths and a healthy operating environment for people doing demanding work.
Set a multi-year roadmap, operating budget, and investment priorities aligned with business risk and technology strategy.
Define meaningful measures of effectiveness, such as detection coverage and validation, telemetry health, alert quality, time to detect and contain, and completion of post-incident improvements.
Communicate security operations performance, material risks, and investment tradeoffs clearly to technical teams and executive leaders.
Work with security and technology partners to meet applicable regulatory and contractual obligations, and provide evidence of operational effectiveness.

Qualifications

Approximately 8 years of experience in technology, including at least 5 years leading security operations, incident response, detection engineering, or closely related teams.
Experience building or evolving security operations capabilities for a complex, global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading significant security incidents and coordinating technical responders and business stakeholders through investigation, containment, and recovery.
Strong technical understanding of detection engineering and security observability, including logging pipelines, detection logic, security analytics, and automation.
Experience applying software engineering practices to security operations, such as version control, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration and deployment.
Experience detecting and responding to threats across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, and application environments.
Experience using threat intelligence and adversary frameworks, such as MITRE ATT&CK, to inform detection priorities and assess coverage.
Experience designing or operating incident response processes informed by frameworks such as NIST, and measuring whether those processes work in practice.
Sound judgment in balancing security outcomes, operational workload, cost, privacy, and business impact.
Ability to influence across organizational boundaries, communicate clearly under pressure, and translate technical risk into actionable business decisions.
A track record of developing people and creating inclusive, accountable teams.

Valuable Additional Experience

Building or scaling purple-team, threat-hunting, or detection validation programs.
Applying AI and automation to security operations with appropriate testing, oversight, and access controls.
Working with managed detection and response providers, incident response partners, or globally distributed operations.
Investigating threats involving software supply chains, development pipelines, and machine or service identities.

must haves

Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.

Additional Notes

Authorization to work in Canada is required for this role.

Compensation And Benefits Package

lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from  $196,600 - $258,100
annually
; the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program and equity offerings , subject to program eligibility requirements.  

At Lululemon, Investing In Our People Is a Top Priority. We Believe That When Life Works, Work Works. We Strive To Be The Place Where Inclusive Leaders Come To Develop And Enable All To Be Well. Recognizing Our Teams For Their Performance And Dedication, Other Components Of Our Total Rewards Offerings Include Support Of Career Development, Wellbeing, And Personal Growth

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.

new_jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The lululemon cybersecurity team helps protect the trust our guests, employees, and partners place in us. We work across technology and the business to understand risk, build practical security capabilities, and enable teams to move quickly and responsibly. We are looking for a Director of Security Operations to lead our Security Incident Response Team (SIRT), Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and Detection Engineering capabilities. This leader will build an operation that treats detections as software: versioned, tested, measurable, and continuously improved.

Core Responsibilities

You will lead a global team of security engineers, analysts, threat hunters, intelligence practitioners, and incident responders. You will set the strategy and operating model for detecting, investigating, and responding to threats across lululemon’s technology environment. You are as comfortable discussing telemetry and detection logic with engineers as you are explaining business impact and response decisions to executives. You know that effective security operations is not measured by how many alerts a team can generate. It is measured by how reliably we identify meaningful threats, respond to them, and improve the systems around us.

Lead incident response

Own the SIRT strategy, incident response lifecycle, and operational readiness across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, network, and application environments.
Lead coordination during significant incidents, establishing clear decision-making, escalation, communications, and recovery processes.
Partner with technology teams, Legal, Privacy, Communications, Risk, and other stakeholders to manage incidents and their business impact.
Run exercises and post-incident reviews that result in owned, tracked improvements to detection, response, and resilience.
Establish a sustainable global coverage model, including on-call and external partnerships where appropriate.

Build detection as code

Set the direction for a detection engineering program that manages detection logic, queries, rules, and response workflows as version-controlled code.
Establish engineering practices for peer review, automated testing, deployment, documentation, tuning, and retirement of detections.
Use threat modeling, incident learnings, threat intelligence, and adversary behavior to prioritize detection coverage against meaningful risks.
Validate detections continuously through simulation, replay, purple teaming, and other appropriate testing methods.
Reduce alert fatigue by improving signal quality, enriching context, and automating repeatable work while retaining human judgment for consequential decisions.

Own security observability

Define the telemetry strategy needed to investigate threats across identities, systems, applications, cloud services, and data flows.
Partner with engineering and platform teams to build reliable, secure, and cost-conscious telemetry pipelines, including clear ownership, data quality, retention, and access controls.
Identify and address visibility gaps, including those created by changes in infrastructure, SaaS adoption, and emerging technologies.
Guide the evolution and consolidation of security operations tooling, including decisions about what to build, buy, retain, or retire.

Turn intelligence into action

Lead a threat intelligence capability that identifies and communicates threats relevant to lululemon’s business, technology, and operating environment.
Translate intelligence into prioritized detections, hunts, defensive improvements, and incident readiness.
Build trusted relationships with industry peers, partners, and relevant information-sharing communities.

Build the team and program

Hire, develop, and retain a diverse, high-performing team. Create clear career paths and a healthy operating environment for people doing demanding work.
Set a multi-year roadmap, operating budget, and investment priorities aligned with business risk and technology strategy.
Define meaningful measures of effectiveness, such as detection coverage and validation, telemetry health, alert quality, time to detect and contain, and completion of post-incident improvements.
Communicate security operations performance, material risks, and investment tradeoffs clearly to technical teams and executive leaders.
Work with security and technology partners to meet applicable regulatory and contractual obligations, and provide evidence of operational effectiveness.

Qualifications

Approximately 8 years of experience in technology, including at least 5 years leading security operations, incident response, detection engineering, or closely related teams.
Experience building or evolving security operations capabilities for a complex, global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading significant security incidents and coordinating technical responders and business stakeholders through investigation, containment, and recovery.
Strong technical understanding of detection engineering and security observability, including logging pipelines, detection logic, security analytics, and automation.
Experience applying software engineering practices to security operations, such as version control, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration and deployment.
Experience detecting and responding to threats across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, and application environments.
Experience using threat intelligence and adversary frameworks, such as MITRE ATT&CK, to inform detection priorities and assess coverage.

new_jobs.title: Director, Central Quality Audit, Pharmacovigilance
new_jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.
Metrics and Reporting: Define and track PV audit KPIs, ensuring visibility of compliance risks and trends to leadership.
System Ownership: Manage audit-related modules within the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including support of configuration, UAT, and documentation.
Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of 3–5 auditors, providing coaching, mentorship, and performance management.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with PV Operations, Quality, and Regulatory teams to ensure audit outcomes drive continuous improvement.
Strategic Influence: Contribute to policy development and influence PV compliance strategy across the organization.

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including team development and performance management.
Qualified Lead Auditor with active certification.
Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.
Minimum of 5 years’ experience driving Global programs to resolve quality compliance issues (directly).
Experience with Pharmaceutical QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to cGMP, GDP, GPvP, GCP and GLP.

Desired Characteristics

Experience with Medical Device QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820 and ISO 13485.
Prior Veeva and TrackWise Digital experience a plus.
Prior health authority experience a plus.
IRCA, ASQ (CQE, CQA, etc.) and/or Lean Certification a plus (green belt, black belt).
Extensive experience in the Medica Device and Pharmaceutical industry.
Understanding of product quality improvement using tools such as Six Sigma, DFR.
Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
Exceptional conflict-resolution skills.
Ability to interface with top organizational leadership and internal and external customers, responding in a professional manner.
Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to prioritize and drive multiple programs.
Ability to energize others by building a connection with the team through personal involvement and trust, providing feedback and coaching to develop others, and accountability of actions.
Strong oral and written communication skills in English.
Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others.
Ability to travel globally up to 15%.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership –always with unyielding integrity.

Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. For U.S. based positions only, the pay range for this position is $142,400.00-$213,600.00 Annual. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including skills, qualifications, experience and location. In addition, this position may also be eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). GE HealthCare offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, and tuition reimbursement.
